To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed a novel and robust method for de novo generation of SATACs by induced large scale satellite DNA amplification.
the inductive generation of SATACs via induced large scale satellite DNA amplification is a feasible approach to generate artificial chromosomes in mammalian cells.
satellite DNA based artificial chromosome (SATACs), generated by the inductive method, are a safe, stable and efficient vector system for the delivery of transgenes in mammalian cells and animals.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a safe and efficient gene transfer technology for gene therapy.
the development of a new vector system for gene delivery.
the development and characterization of a novel vector system for gene technology applications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SATACs can be generated by the inductive method and are stable in mammalian cells and in mice.

the in vivo "satellite DNA based" artificial chromosome generation approach is a very promising and powerful method to generate large artificial chromosomes that can be used as a non-integrating, large carrying capacity vector for gene technology.
the in vivo "satellite DNA induction" method for SATACs generation is a simple, robust and reliable method that is reproducible and can be used in a variety of mammalian cell types.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a method to induce the de novo formation of artificial chromosomes from an episomal plasmid.
the inductive approach is an efficient way to generate large amounts of SATACs in vivo.

the in vivo "in duction" approach for the generation of SATACs can be applied in any mammalian cell line and that the amplification of the satellite DNA is a stochastic process that is influenced by the amount of exogenously added satellite DNA, the copy number of the endogenous chromosome and the presence of centromeric sequences in the cell line.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the generation of SATACs can be accomplished with relative ease and speed by the use of a combination of molecular, cellular and animal manipulation techniques.
a de novo generated SATAC can be efficiently used for the production of therapeutic proteins in mammalian cells.
SATACs can be generated by the de novo amplification of a satellite DNA based minichromosome.
